DIAGNOSIS READY: Auricular Concha Cartilage Perichondritis (infection of the cartilage and perichondrium in the ear canal, likely triggered by trauma from earring insertion post-tympanoplasty).

The normal measurements and lack of reported discharge or fluid suggest the graft itself is intact and there is no active otitis media. The specific nature of the "shooting" pain upon touching the ear cartilage with an earring is highly suggestive of local inflammation of the cartilage lining. Do you have a history of diabetes or are you currently on immunosuppressive medications that might predispose you to this infection?
